F1.text: Major — `coordinator/overnight/lane_driver.py:724–725`: Every nonzero `launchctl` result means “stopped,” including permission, domain, or IPC query failures. This can falsely alarm for a healthy job. Only service-not-found should mean unloaded; other query failures should use the unavailable-signal fallback.

F2.text: Major — `coordinator/overnight/lane_driver.py:734`: Missing numeric exit status defaults to success. A job reporting `last terminating signal` rather than `last exit code` is therefore treated as healthy after a crash, suppressing a real alarm. Handle signal termination and preserve unknown status.

F3.text: Major — `coordinator/overnight/lane_driver.py:741`: The terminating-signal regex accepts only an integer. Descriptive launchctl output such as `last terminating signal = Killed: 9` becomes `signal=0`. With no exit code and a fresh log, the fallback suppresses the alarm despite termination evidence. Parse both formats and cover the descriptive format in the regression fixture.
